paragraphs.en: At the neighborhood clinic, a gentleman introduced himself as “Sir Andrew,” then laughed and said that a surname was quite enough. A young tenant beside him seemed less relaxed: her landlord had complained about the time she spent helping an elderly uncle. The nurse asked each visitor to describe a difficulty in ordinary language. “Somebody always speaks on behalf of my family,” the tenant said, “but nobody asks what I need.” The clinic’s new program was intended to change that pattern.
paragraphs.zh: 社区诊所里，一位先生自称“安德鲁爵士”，随后笑着说只叫姓氏就够了。旁边的年轻租客却不那么放松：房东抱怨她花太多时间照顾年迈的叔叔。护士请来访者用日常语言描述困难。租客说：“总有人代表我家发言，却没人问我需要什么。”诊所的新项目正是要改变这种状况。

paragraphs.en: An older lady explained that her spouse had pain in a hip and one leg. He could hear poorly in one ear and worried about every unfamiliar word. “Is this a bone problem or a nerve problem?” she asked. Rather than discuss an organ as though it existed apart from a person, the doctor demonstrated a joint movement and checked the heel carefully. He also asked about sleep, work, and the companion who provided daily help. Listening supplied information that a short medical profile could not capture.
paragraphs.zh: 一位年长女士说，配偶的髋部和一条腿疼痛，一侧耳朵听力较差，也容易被陌生术语吓住。“这是骨头的问题，还是神经的问题？”她问。医生没有把器官当作与人无关的物件来讨论，而是演示关节运动，仔细检查脚后跟，并询问睡眠、工作，以及每天提供照护的伴侣。倾听带来的信息，无法全部浓缩到简短的病情简介里。

paragraphs.en: A youngster with a loose tooth watched while his cousin practiced breathing exercises for a lung condition. His twin sister pointed to her nose, her lip, and her tongue, curious about how the mouth produced speech. Their mother, a housewife, said that explaining health at home was harder than expected. A friendly guy from the library offered illustrated materials. They showed that one need not live alone as a bachelor with abundant free time to learn: information could be shared in small moments, without blaming oneself for every mistake.
paragraphs.zh: 一个牙齿松动的孩子看着表亲为肺部问题练习呼吸。双胞胎妹妹指着鼻子、嘴唇和舌头，好奇嘴巴怎样发出语言。身为家庭主妇的母亲说，在家解释健康知识比想象中困难。图书馆一位亲切的工作人员拿来配图资料。这些资料说明，学习并不需要成为空闲充裕的单身汉：知识可以在零碎时间里交流，也不必为每次犯错自责。

paragraphs.en: The program also welcomed newcomers who feared being treated as alien to local life. A civilian who had left a distant region described the customs of his tribe and a healing practice passed down by an ancestor. The staff neither mocked the belief nor accepted it without evidence. “A tradition can be yours or mine,” the coordinator said, “but a safe clinic must be ours.” A volunteer called her mate to translate, taking care not to turn a difference in language into a difference in respect.
paragraphs.zh: 项目也欢迎那些担心自己不被本地接纳的新来者。一位从远方迁来的平民讲述所属部落的习俗，以及祖辈传下来的治疗方法。工作人员既不嘲笑这种信念，也不在缺乏证据时照单全收。协调员说：“传统可以属于你，也可以属于我，但安全的诊所必须属于我们共同。”志愿者请同伴来翻译，注意不让语言差异变成尊重程度的差异。

paragraphs.en: During a public demonstration, a spectator jokingly called the nurse a queen of patience. She replied that mankind had no sole owner of knowledge. Anybody could notice when a relative was struggling to swallow, yet persistent throat pain required professional assessment. She invited the folk gathered at the rear of the room to come closer. The program could not prevent every illness in their offspring, but it could make seeking help less frightening. Care began when people felt entitled to ask a question. An old poster had celebrated masculine endurance, but this program recognized that asking for assistance could also be an act of responsibility. Staff recorded which explanations had helped and which had confused visitors, allowing the next session to reflect actual experience instead of repeating an attractive program exactly as originally imagined.
paragraphs.zh: 公开演示中，一位旁观者打趣说护士是“耐心女王”。她回答，人类的知识并不由某个人独占。任何人都可能发现亲属吞咽困难，但持续的喉咙疼痛需要专业评估。她邀请聚在房间后部的人靠近些。项目无法预防下一代的所有疾病，却能降低求助时的恐惧。照护始于人们觉得自己有权提问。旧海报曾歌颂男性的忍耐力，但这个项目认识到，寻求帮助同样可以体现责任。工作人员记录哪些解释有帮助、哪些让来访者困惑，使下一次活动根据实际体验调整，而不是原封不动重复最初想象中的漂亮方案。
